name: Programming & Data Structures (C)
description: C programming, recursion and the classic data structures GATE tests: arrays, lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps and hashing.

nodes.name: C basics
nodes.desc: Types, integer representation, operators, precedence and expression evaluation in C (and the Pascal-style snippets older papers use).
nodes.summary: You will be able to predict the result of C expressions using types, integer representation, operator precedence and evaluation rules.
topics: Basic data types and their sizes

nodes.name: Loops & control flow
nodes.desc: if/switch, for/while/do-while, break and continue; tracing loops and reasoning with loop invariants.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace C loops and branches accurately and reason about their behaviour using loop invariants.

nodes.name: Functions & scope
nodes.desc: Function calls, block and file scope, lifetime, and static variables that keep their value between calls.
nodes.summary: You will be able to determine which variable a name refers to and how long it lives, including static variables across calls.

nodes.name: Parameter passing
nodes.desc: Call by value versus simulated call by reference through pointers; why swap(a, b) does not work.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace call by value and simulated call by reference in C and explain why a naive swap fails.
topics: Passing pointers to modify caller data
Arrays decaying to pointers in calls
Call by reference and call by name

nodes.name: Macros & linking
nodes.desc: The preprocessor and macros, compilation units, linkers, loaders, relocation and external symbols.
nodes.summary: You will be able to expand preprocessor macros correctly and explain how compilation units are linked, loaded and relocated.

nodes.name: Pointers
nodes.desc: Addresses, dereferencing, pointers to pointers, aliasing and how pointers make C functions modify caller data.
nodes.summary: You will be able to declare, dereference and trace pointers, including pointers to pointers and aliasing.

nodes.name: Pointer arithmetic
nodes.desc: Pointer arithmetic, the array–pointer relationship, and indexing multi-dimensional arrays through pointers.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute pointer arithmetic results and index one- and multi-dimensional arrays through pointers.
topics: Pointers to arrays versus arrays of pointers

nodes.name: Strings & structs
nodes.desc: Null-terminated strings, character arrays versus string literals, structs and pointers to structs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to manipulate null-terminated strings and structs in C, including pointers to structs.
topics: Pointers to structs and the arrow operator

nodes.name: Dynamic memory
nodes.desc: malloc and free, heap versus stack storage, dangling pointers and memory leaks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to allocate and free heap memory in C and recognise dangling pointers and memory leaks.

nodes.name: Recursion
nodes.desc: Recursive functions in C: base cases, tracing output, and counting calls.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write recursive C functions with correct base cases and trace their output and number of calls.

nodes.name: Recursion trees
nodes.desc: Drawing recursion trees, counting calls and stack depth, and mixing recursion with pointer or static parameters.
nodes.summary: You will be able to draw recursion trees for C programs and count calls and stack depth, even with static or pointer parameters.

nodes.name: Arrays
nodes.desc: One- and two-dimensional arrays, in-place algorithms on arrays and their loop invariants.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write and reason about array algorithms in C, including in-place updates and their loop invariants.

nodes.name: Array addressing
nodes.desc: Row-major and column-major layout, address formulas, and triangular or sparse matrix storage.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute element addresses in row-major and column-major layouts and store triangular and sparse matrices compactly.

nodes.name: Linked lists
nodes.desc: Singly, doubly and circular linked lists: insertion, deletion, reversal and pointer manipulation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to implement and trace singly, doubly and circular linked lists, including insertion, deletion and reversal.
topics: Insertion at head, tail and middle

nodes.name: Stacks & queues
nodes.desc: Stack and queue ADTs on arrays and lists, circular queues, queues from stacks and stack permutations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to implement stacks and queues on arrays and lists and reason about circular queues and stack permutations.
topics: Circular queue full and empty conditions

nodes.name: Expression evaluation
nodes.desc: Infix to postfix conversion, postfix evaluation and parenthesis matching with a stack.
nodes.summary: You will be able to convert infix to postfix, evaluate postfix expressions and check parenthesis matching with a stack.
topics: Infix to postfix with operator precedence

nodes.name: Binary trees
nodes.desc: Binary and n-ary trees: representation, recursive algorithms on trees, and their properties.
nodes.summary: You will be able to represent binary and n-ary trees in C and write recursive algorithms over them.

nodes.name: Tree traversals
nodes.desc: Preorder, inorder, postorder and level order traversals, and rebuilding a tree from two traversals.
nodes.summary: You will be able to perform preorder, inorder, postorder and level-order traversals and rebuild a tree from two traversals.

nodes.name: Tree properties
nodes.desc: Counting nodes, leaves and heights in full, complete and n-ary trees; proofs by induction.
nodes.summary: You will be able to count nodes, leaves and heights in full, complete and n-ary trees and prove such facts by induction.
topics: Full, complete and perfect binary trees

nodes.name: Binary search trees
nodes.desc: BST search, insertion and deletion, traversal orders of a BST and counting BSTs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to search, insert into and delete from binary search trees and count BSTs on n keys.

nodes.name: Balanced BSTs
nodes.desc: AVL trees, rotations and height bounds of balanced search trees.
nodes.summary: You will be able to keep a BST balanced with AVL rotations and compute height bounds for balanced search trees.
topics: LL, RR, LR and RL rotations
Minimum nodes for a given height

nodes.name: Heaps
nodes.desc: Binary min- and max-heaps stored in arrays; the heap property and priority queues.
nodes.summary: You will be able to store binary min- and max-heaps in arrays and use them as priority queues.
topics: Checking whether an array is a heap

nodes.name: Heap operations
nodes.desc: Insert, delete, heapify and linear-time build-heap, d-ary heaps and their costs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace heap insertion, deletion and heapify, build a heap in linear time and analyse d-ary heaps.

nodes.name: Hashing
nodes.desc: Hash functions, hash tables and load factor.
nodes.summary: You will be able to design simple hash functions and reason about hash tables and their load factor.

nodes.name: Collision resolution
nodes.desc: Chaining, linear probing and double hashing: tracing insertions and probe sequences.
nodes.summary: You will be able to trace insertions and probe sequences under chaining, linear probing and double hashing.

nodes.name: Graph representation
nodes.desc: Adjacency matrices and adjacency lists, their space costs and simple queries on them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to represent graphs with adjacency matrices and lists and compare their space and query costs.
topics: Space costs for sparse and dense graphs
